convention: anthropics/skills/skill-creator evals.json — two kinds. `kind:"trigger"` fixtures carry `should_trigger` for description-optimisation (train/held-out trigger accuracy). `kind:"behavioural"` fixtures carry a `tier` (M/D/R) and `expectations[]` asserting the skill applies / reasons / declines correctly on a salvaged Reagent→re-frame.ui fixture input.
notes: Positives target Reagent-view→re-frame.ui prompts on an already-re-frame2 app (compiled views, reg-view→defview, deref-drop, adopt the experimental substrate). Negatives target the DIFFERENT v1→v2 events/subs/db migration (re-frame-migration), authoring on re-frame2 (re-frame2), greenfield (re-frame2-setup), live runtime (re-frame2-pair), and the first-class 'stay on Reagent' non-goal. Behavioural inputs are drawn from the shelved W1 migrator's golden fixtures; the M/D/R trio is the tier-coverage floor the bead requires.

evals.name: m-transform-defview-sub-lift
evals.prompt:
Convert this to re-frame.ui:
(defn price [amt cur] [:button {:on-click #(dispatch [:buy amt])} @(subscribe [:total])])
(defn app [] [:div [price 1 2]])
expectations: Rewrites the header to (ui/defview price [{:keys [amt cur]}] ...) — positional params become a destructured prop map (MIG-01).
Rewrites the call site atomically to [price {:amt 1 :cur 2}] in the same change (MIG-01).
Drops the deref: @(subscribe [:total]) becomes (sub [:total]) (MIG-02).
Lifts the handler: {:on-click #(dispatch [:buy amt])} becomes {:on-click [:buy amt]} (MIG-04).
Adds the require [re-frame.ui :as ui :refer [defview sub]] (MIG-24) and cites the MIG ids for each change.
Does NOT treat the event vector [:buy amt] or the query vector [:total] as hiccup to respell/spread.

evals.name: d-decide-form2-local-state
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent view to re-frame.ui:
(defn dropdown [] (r/with-let [open? (r/atom false)] [:div {:on-click #(reset! open? true)} (when @open? [:ul])]))
expectations: Recognises Form-2 / with-let view-local state (MIG-16) and does NOT silently rewrite the view.
Reasons about the decision — is this PRODUCT state (→ app-db: an event + a sub, a dataflow change to name for the author) or EPHEMERAL UI state (→ the host-local `local`)?
If ephemeral, maps to `local`'s three-tuple: @open? → value, (reset! open? v) → (set! v), (swap! open? f) → (update! f) — and explicitly avoids (set! (f open?)) as last-write-wins.
Holds the WHOLE view until the decision is made (cardinal rule 2), rather than converting some sites and leaving others.
Does not reach into the dataflow layer itself; it names the reg-event/reg-sub for the author when app-db is the answer.

evals.name: d-route-ssr-static-vs-hydrate
evals.prompt:
Migrate this to re-frame.ui:
(ns app.render (:require [reagent.dom.server :as s]))
(defn render-page [] (s/render-to-string [app]))
expectations: Treats MIG-23 as a shipped SSR transform, NOT a decline — ui/render-static and ui/hydrate-root have shipped.
Routes by intent: a static-page (non-hydrating) render maps to (ui/render-static [app-root]) — the compiled counterpart of React's renderToStaticMarkup.
Names the SSR-then-hydrate path as the alternative and asks which the app wants: re-frame.ssr/hydrate! (state only, no :render-tree-fn) then ui/hydrate-root (Spec 011).
Keeps the caveat: views using refs/effects need ui/client-only (or restructure) for the pure server phase.
Does NOT hold the view as an unshipped capability gap.

evals.name: r-decline-reagent-introspection
evals.prompt:
Convert this view to re-frame.ui:
(defn thing [] [:div (str (r/current-component))])
expectations: Declines — Reagent component-introspection / scheduler calls have no compiled equivalent (MIG-35).
Warns that r/current-component still COMPILES after conversion and fails/returns nil at runtime, so the build gate will not catch it.

Keeps the view on Reagent, or restructures away from the introspection (props/children the view already receives); does NOT equate the schedulers r/next-tick / r/after-render with ui/effect — those stay on Reagent unless the author redesigns phase/frequency/ownership.

evals.name: d-mig18-handler-split
evals.prompt:
Migrate this view to re-frame.ui:
(ns f (:require [re-frame.core :refer [dispatch]]))
(defn save-btn [] [:button {:on-click (fn [e] (.preventDefault e) (when @dirty? (dispatch [:save])))} "Save"])
expectations: Recognises MIG-18 — the handler is not one of the three clean shapes (mixed guard + dispatch), so it is a judgment call, not an automatic lift.
Routes the guarded dispatch to ui/event (a nil return means no dispatch — the guard expressed as data-with-a-filter), not a bare fn.
Notes that a converted defview has no ambient dispatch; imperative dispatch would go through (ui/dispatch-fn) in the view body.
Holds/decides the WHOLE view (the guard reads view-local state, coupling it to the MIG-16 state decision) — no half-migrated body.

evals.name: m-negative-bare-symbol-not-spread
evals.prompt:
Migrate to re-frame.ui:
(defn item [t] [:li t])
(defn lst [ts] [:ul (for [t ts] ^{:key t} [item t])])
expectations: Converts item and lst to ui/defview and moves ^{:key t} to a :key prop (MIG-07): [item {:key t :t t}].
Does NOT treat the bare symbol child in [:li t] as a props map — `t` is content, never (ui/spread t) (the bare-symbol trap).
Leaves the plain hiccup structure otherwise unchanged (MIG-14).

evals.name: d-mig17-lifecycle-rehome-unmount
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to re-frame.ui:
(ns app.editor (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom]))
(defn editor []
  (let [{:keys [dispatch]} (rf/capture-frame)]
    (r/create-class
     {:component-did-mount    (fn [this] (.focus (rdom/dom-node this)))
      :component-will-unmount (fn [_] (dispatch [:resource/release]))
      :reagent-render         (fn [] [editor-form])})))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 lifecycle and decomposes each body into host/DOM work vs domain work — a judgment call held WHOLE (cardinal rule 2), not an automatic rewrite.

Routes the host/DOM work (focus the node on mount) to (effect :connect …), with the body's RETURN value as the cleanup — a trailing (fn [] …), NOT the React useEffect shape (a setup fn that returns a cleanup fn), which compiles but silently never runs.

Recognises there is NO dispatch-at-unmount in native re-frame.ui: (ui/dispatch-fn) fails loud at disconnect with :rf.error/dispatch-disconnected (the leaked-listener law), so an effect cleanup is NOT a place to smuggle the domain release.

Re-homes the unmount domain work (the [:resource/release] dispatch) OUT of the view — to the causal events that end the resource's life — and names those events / the minting owner for the author (cardinal rule 5); the migrated view becomes a pure defview that owns no resource lifetime.

Does NOT invent a view-owned / component-presence resource lifetime (there is none in re-frame.ui — liveness never re-enters through the view); here the owner is app-minted (route-minted, released by the causal events), so the read re-homes to that causal owner. When a resource has no causal event bounding its life, an ownerless ensure (cause-only, GC-eligible) is the valid tool, never a view that owns a lifetime.

evals.name: d-mig17-measure-before-paint-layout-effect
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to re-frame.ui:
(ns app.popover (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom]))
(defn popover [anchor]
  (r/create-class
   {:component-did-mount (fn [this] (place! (rdom/dom-node this) (measure anchor)))
    :reagent-render      (fn [a] [:div.popover])}))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 and that :component-did-mount here does MEASURE-then-mutate BEFORE paint (reads geometry to place the popover), so a passive effect would measure a frame late and flicker.
Does NOT route this to (effect :connect …); routes it to ui/ref + re-frame.ui.react/use-layout-effect (the measure-before-paint door), preserving the pre-paint semantics component-did-mount gave.

Uses the React interop shape for the layout-effect hook — (react/use-layout-effect (fn [] … cleanup-or-nil) deps) with a setup fn returning a cleanup fn or nil — NOT ui/effect's body-return shape, and reads the node via (.-current (ui/ref)).
Keeps ordinary listeners / focus / deferrable host work on the passive effect — the split is only for the narrow pre-paint case, not a wholesale hooks migration.
Holds/decides the WHOLE view (cardinal rule 2) rather than half-migrating it.

evals.name: r-scheduler-not-effect
evals.prompt:
Migrate this view to re-frame.ui:
(ns f (:require [reagent.core :as r]))
(defn flasher [] (r/after-render #(flash!)) [:div "hi"])
expectations: Does NOT equate r/after-render (or r/next-tick) with ui/effect — they are Reagent one-shot render-queue schedulers (fire immediately before the next flush / immediately after queued renders, even when nothing renders), not component-owned passive post-commit effect work (MIG-35).
Keeps the scheduler call R-tier: holds the view on Reagent unless the author EXPLICITLY redesigns the work's phase, frequency, and ownership (a deliberate re-model, not a rename).
Warns that the call still COMPILES after conversion and misbehaves only at runtime, so the build gate will not catch a silent swap to effect.

evals.name: d-mig17-did-update-dep-keyed-effect
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to re-frame.ui:
(ns app.chart (:require [reagent.core :as r]))
(defn vega-chart [_spec]
  (let [el (atom nil) view (atom nil)]
    (r/create-class
     {:component-did-mount    (fn [this] (let [[_ s] (r/argv this)] (.then (js/vegaEmbed @el (clj->js s)) (fn [res] (reset! view (.-view res))))))
      :component-did-update   (fn [this _ _ _] (let [[_ s] (r/argv this)] (.then (js/vegaEmbed @el (clj->js s)) (fn [res] (some-> @view .finalize) (reset! view (.-view res))))))
      :component-will-unmount (fn [_] (some-> @view .finalize))
      :reagent-render         (fn [_] [:div {:ref (fn [e] (reset! el e))}])})))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 and decomposes each lifecycle body — a judgment call held WHOLE (cardinal rule 2), not an automatic rewrite.

Routes :component-did-update (re-feed the imperative library when the spec prop changes) to the dependency-keyed (effect [spec] …) — runs its body after commit whenever the dep changes (compared by rf=), with the library-update recipe inside (finalize the old view, then embed the new); keeps the dep narrow.

Does NOT collapse this did-update to a subscription/Form-1 — the library does NOT re-render on data change, so the effect is load-bearing; contrasts it with a did-update that ONLY reads data to re-render (that one IS the subscription/Form-1 case, and the lifecycle disappears).

Routes :component-did-mount host work to (effect :connect …) and the :component-will-unmount disposal to that effect's trailing-fn cleanup (the body's RETURN value is the cleanup, NOT the React useEffect setup-returns-cleanup shape, which compiles but never runs the setup).
Consistent with reagent-slim FORM-3.md §6 (:component-did-update → dependency-keyed effect); this is the re-com-relevant decision (re-com's Form-3 sites use :component-did-update).

evals.name: r-mig17-snapshot-pair-holds-on-form3
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to re-frame.ui:
(ns app.log (:require [reagent.core :as r]))
(defn scroll-log [_entries]
  (let [c (atom nil)]
    (r/create-class
     {:get-snapshot-before-update (fn [_ _ _] (when-let [el @c] {:top (.-scrollTop el)}))
      :component-did-update        (fn [_ _ _ snap] (when-let [el @c] (when-let [t (:top snap)] (set! (.-scrollTop el) t))))
      :reagent-render              (fn [entries] [:div.log {:ref (fn [e] (reset! c e))} (for [x entries] ^{:key (:id x)} [:div (:text x)])])})))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 with the paired :get-snapshot-before-update + :component-did-update protocol (pre-commit measure → post-commit restore — scroll restoration).

HOLDS the whole view on reagent-slim Form-3: there is NO native passive-effect or hook equivalent, because use-layout-effect runs AFTER React mutates the DOM and so cannot read the pre-mutation geometry; the pre-commit half of the protocol has no native door.
Does NOT route the snapshot protocol to (effect …) or use-layout-effect as if equivalent — that would silently lose the pre-commit measurement.

Explains this paired protocol is exactly why the reagent-slim 7-key cap keeps :get-snapshot-before-update (FORM-3.md §5/§6), so staying on Form-3 is the correct answer, not a lossy rewrite — held WHOLE (cardinal rule 2).

evals.name: d-mig17-did-catch-error-boundary
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 error boundary to re-frame.ui:
(ns app.boundary (:require [reagent.core :as r]))
(defn boundary [_]
  (let [err (r/atom nil)]
    (r/create-class
     {:component-did-catch (fn [_ e _info] (js/console.error e) (reset! err e))
      :reagent-render      (fn [child] (if @err [:div.fallback "Something went wrong."] child))})))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 :component-did-catch and routes it to the SHIPPED (ui/error-boundary {:fallback view :reset-key val :on-error [:ev …]} child) when its logging/recovery semantics fit — NOT a decline.

Maps the local r/atom fallback flip to the boundary's :fallback view (which renders with :error and cannot recursively dispatch), the console log / domain notification to :on-error (dispatches AFTER the failing commit), and clears the caught error by changing :reset-key (retry).
Notes React catches only render/lifecycle throws BELOW the boundary — not event-handler or async errors, which keep their own typed paths.
Holds honestly: when ui/error-boundary's semantics do NOT fit, the view stays on reagent-slim Form-3 (:component-did-catch + a local r/atom) or is redesigned — consistent with FORM-3.md §6.
Does NOT invent an unshipped API — ui/error-boundary is a shipped re-frame.ui template form (verify against the re-frame.ui exports).
